preregistration.revision_reason: adversarial audit established that PyPal synchronization used oracle-related frame correspondences and that the 1 ms diagnostic set contains no negative pairs

derived_fields.observer_id: observer token parsed from the selected ZIP member name

same_event.condition: distinct observers and equal complete oracle_event_key values
same_event.interpretation: the two observations represent the same publisher-keyed transmission event

different_event.condition: distinct observations have different complete oracle_event_key values in a separately designed evaluation pair set
different_event.interpretation: the two observations represent different publisher-keyed transmission events; the synchronized-time diagnostic does not supply these pairs

unknown.condition: the pair is not in an independently justified evaluation set, has an incomplete oracle key, or cannot satisfy the registered integrity checks
unknown.interpretation: no same-event or different-event conclusion is admitted

synchronized_time_diagnostic.reason: PyPal fitted the synchronized time axis from common reference frames matched with a composite key that included source MAC and sequence number

metrics.name: observation_count
metrics.numerator: parsed rows across all selected members

metrics.name: multi_observer_event_count
metrics.numerator: oracle events observed by at least two distinct observers

metrics.name: all_observer_event_count
metrics.numerator: oracle events observed by all ten distinct observers

metrics.name: positive_cross_observer_pair_count
metrics.numerator: sum over oracle events of n_distinct_observers choose 2

metrics.name: duplicate_event_key_count
metrics.numerator: repeated oracle_event_key values within an observer

metrics.name: contradictory_invariant_event_count
metrics.numerator: oracle events having more than one event_invariant_fields tuple

metrics.name: synchronized_time_pair_count
metrics.numerator: all emitted cross-observer pairs inside the inclusive 1 ms diagnostic window

metrics.name: positive_synchronized_time_coverage
metrics.numerator: same_event pairs emitted by the diagnostic

metrics.name: synchronized_time_positive_prevalence
metrics.interpretation: leakage diagnostic only; not predictive performance

failure_gates: archive identity or selected member inventory differs from the registered source
a selected member does not have the exact registered nine-column header
a selected row is malformed or has an incomplete oracle event key
any exact expected structural count differs
any observer contains a duplicate oracle event key
any oracle event has contradictory invariant metadata
the synchronized-time diagnostic differs from the registered all-positive result
any forbidden predictive field reaches predictive input
the complete run is partitioned or used to fit a threshold
two identical executions do not serialize byte-identical reports

blockers.claim: predictive accuracy, calibration, or threshold selection
blockers.blocked_by: there is one locked publisher experiment and no independent train, calibration, or test acquisition

blockers.claim: timestamp as candidate blocking or a predictive feature
blockers.blocked_by: PyPal derived the synchronized time axis from same-frame composite correspondences including source MAC and sequence number
independent labeled acquisitions spanning other runs, distances, transmitters, sites, and times are absent
the oracle labels publisher-keyed transmission events, not durable hardware or owner identity

limitations: The campaign covers only the complete 1 m slice of one Sorbonne outdoor experiment.
All ten observers belong to the same acquisition, so observer pairs are dependent rather than independent examples.
The oracle establishes equality under Source_MAC_address plus Sequence_number within this run; it does not establish cross-run or cross-corpus identity.
The synchronized 1 ms diagnostic contains no different-event pairs and cannot evaluate a three-way hypothesis reducer.
A later pair-classification campaign needs a separately justified, event-balanced negative set and a packet fingerprint that masks oracle and observer-specific fields.
RSSI and observer identity are deliberately excluded from predictive input even though they may carry acquisition-specific signal.
The campaign is a deterministic oracle and candidate-generation audit, not a fitted-model benchmark.
No confidence interval or generalization estimate is valid from this single locked split.
